Haan, **local pe test kar sakte ho—direct deploy karne ki zarurat nahi**. Deployment se pehle local environment me API endpoints, database connection, environment variables, aur error logs verify kar lo.

Likely flow:

1. Backend locally start karo.
2. Required database/services configure karo.
3. API requests se endpoints test karo.
4. Sab pass hone ke baad staging/production deploy karo.

Exact local commands project ke framework aur configuration dekhke bataye ja sakte hain.

Haan, **existing IAM user ko SES full access dene ki zarurat nahi hai**. README ka broad `AWSLambda_FullAccess` suggestion over-permissioned hai. Best practice: **deployment, Lambda runtime, aur local SES ke credentials alag rakho**.

## 1. Local testing ke liye credentials

Tumhare project `C:\kamlesh\projects\portfolio_api\.env.example` ke according:

| Setting | Local testing |
|---|---|
| `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` | Turso database URL |
| `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` | Turso database auth token |
| `JWT_SECRET` | Minimum 32-character strong random secret |
| `EMAIL_PROVIDER` | `log` |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | Empty |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Empty |

`EMAIL_PROVIDER=log` karne par OTP application logs me print hoga. **Local functional testing ke liye AWS credentials bilkul zarurat nahi.**

```env
EMAIL_PROVIDER=log
```

Actual email deliver test karna ho, tab local AWS identity ko **sirf `ses:SendEmail`** permission dena hoga—`AmazonSESFullAccess` nahi.

Example least-privilege policy:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowPortfolioOtpSending",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "ses:SendEmail",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ses:ap-south-1:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:identity/<verified-domain-or-email>"
    }
  ]
}
```

Local me preferred approach: separate local SES IAM user/role aur `AWS_PROFILE` use karo. Long-lived keys ko `.env` me dalne se better hai.

---

## 2. Production Lambda ke liye SES credentials

Lambda environment me ye variables chahiye:

```env
EMAIL_PROVIDER=ses
AWS_REGION=ap-south-1
SES_FROM_EMAIL=no-reply@yourdomain.com
SES_FROM_NAME=Portfolio Admin
SES_REPLY_TO=you@yourdomain.com
```

Lekin Lambda me ye **empty** rakhne hain:

```env
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=
AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=
```

Code khud Lambda execution role use karta hai. `C:\kamlesh\projects\portfolio_api\internal\email\ses.go` bhi yehi fallback use karta hai.

Lambda execution role ko chahiye:

1. `AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole`
2. Verified sender identity ke liye restricted `ses:SendEmail`
3. SES full access nahi

Turso/JWT secrets Lambda environment variables me set honge; GitHub secrets me unnecessary nahi.

---

## 3. Existing Lambda + ECR IAM user

Existing IAM user ko:

- ECR repository me image push
- Existing Lambda function update

ke liye use kar sakte ho.

**Lekin SES permission us deployment user ko dene ki zarurat nahi.** SES Lambda execution role se chalega.

Recommended separation:

```text
Existing IAM user
└── ECR push
└── Lambda create/update

Lambda execution role
└── CloudWatch logs
└── SES SendEmail only for verified identity

Local SES user/profile
└── SES SendEmail only
```

Agar existing IAM user ki keys GitHub me use karni hain, to:

```text
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
```

GitHub repository secrets me daalne padenge. Lekin static keys vulnerable hain; better option **GitHub Actions → AWS IAM OIDC** hai.

---

## 4. Recommended CI/CD authentication

Sabse secure setup:

```text
GitHub Actions
    ↓ short-lived OIDC token
AWS IAM deployment role
    ↓
ECR push + Lambda update
```

Isme GitHub me long-lived AWS keys store nahi karne padte. Workflow:

```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
```

Aur `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` me deployment role ARN assume hota hai. AWS/GitHub official docs bhi OIDC use karte hain.

Deployment role ko ideally sirf ye capabilities milein:

- Selected ECR repository me image push
- Selected Lambda function create/update
- Lambda execution role ko pass karne ki permission
- Logs/function configuration read

`AWSLambda_FullAccess` aur `AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryFullAccess` broad policies avoid karo.

Current codebase search me `.github/workflows` deployment file nahi mili, although `C:\kamlesh\projects\portfolio_api\README.md` GitHub Actions flow describe karta hai. Isliye deployment ke liye workflow implement/configure karna padega.

---

## 5. SES account requirements

Sirf IAM permission se email deliver nahi hota:

- `SES_FROM_EMAIL` identity verify honi chahiye.
- Sender aur region same SES region me hone chahiye.
- `ap-south-1` ke andar SES **sandbox** hai.
- Sandbox me verified recipients ko email ja sakta hai.
- Arbitrary recipients ke liye account ko SES **production access** request karna padega.
- `AmazonSESFullAccess` dene se production access automatically nahi milta; ye separate SES account status hai.

## Recommended final approach

1. Local pe `EMAIL_PROVIDER=log` use karo.
2. Existing IAM user ko SES full access mat do.
3. Lambda execution role ko restricted `ses:SendEmail` policy do.
4. GitHub deployment ke liye OIDC role banao.
5. Existing IAM user ko sirf initial/manual deployment tak rakho; OIDC setup ke baad keys remove kar do.

Official references:

- [AWS Lambda deployment with GitHub Actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/deploying-github-actions.html)
- [GitHub OIDC authentication for AWS](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/security-harden-deployments/oidc-in-aws)
- [Lambda container image and ECR permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html)
- [SES sending authorization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/sending-authorization-identity-owner-tasks-policy.html)

Koi code/config change apply nahi hua. Remaining: AWS OIDC role aur Lambda execution role ka actual setup. Change applied nahi hua—waiting for next instruction.

**Haan, sahi setup ke baad prod se direct test kar sakte ho—access key/secret key ki zarurat nahi padegi.**

- **Lambda runtime:** AWS automatically **Lambda Execution Role** use karega.
- **GitHub Actions deployment:** **AWS OIDC role** use karo; `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` GitHub secrets me store karne ki zarurat nahi.
- **SES:** Lambda execution role ko sirf `ses:SendEmail` permission dena hoga.
- **Local testing:** `EMAIL_PROVIDER=log` rakho; AWS keys nahi chahiye.

Lekin currently agar workflow static IAM keys use kar raha hai, to abhi unki zarurat padegi. OIDC setup ke baad keys hata sakte ho.

Yeh **AWS Console** me configure karna hai:

### Lambda execution role me SES permission dena

1. **AWS Console** kholo: [console.aws.amazon.com](https://console.aws.amazon.com)
2. **Lambda** select karo.
3. Apni Lambda function kholo — jaise `portfolio-api`.
4. **Configuration → Permissions** par jao.
5. **Execution role** ke samne role link par click karo.
5. Role page me **Add permissions → Create policy** select karo.
6. **JSON** tab choose karke ye policy paste karo:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowPortfolioOtpSending",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "ses:SendEmail",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ses:ap-south-1:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:identity/<VERIFIED_DOMAIN_OR_EMAIL>"
    }
  ]
}
```

7. `AWS_ACCOUNT_ID` aur verified SES identity replace karke policy create karo.

Agar Lambda function abhi create nahi hui, to execution role pehle Lambda function create karne par banta hai. **AmazonSESFullAccess mat select karna.** SES identity bhi separately verify honi chahiye.

Change applied nahi hua—AWS console instructions diye gaye hain.
